source: National Park Service, public archives and local historical institutions
note: Selected documented regional events. Pins identify surviving sites, commemorative markers or labeled reference areas; they are not complete event boundaries.

properties.title: Battle of St. Louis / Fort San Carlos
properties.description: Spanish soldiers and local militia defended St. Louis against a British-led attack during the American Revolution. Resistance centered on Fort San Carlos; fighting and raids extended outside the settlement.
properties.locationAccuracy: Nearby commemorative marker; not an exact battlefield boundary. The fort no longer survives.
properties.locationBasis: Nearby commemorative marker; not an exact battlefield boundary. The fort no longer survives.

properties.title: Fort Belle Fontaine established
properties.description: The U.S. Army established a military post on the Missouri River. The original riverside site was later lost to channel changes; a replacement fort was built on the bluff.
properties.locationAccuracy: Present-day park reference point. The original 1805 fort site was destroyed by changes in the river; this pin does not mark its exact footprint.
properties.locationBasis: Present-day park reference point. The original 1805 fort site was destroyed by changes in the river; this pin does not mark its exact footprint.
properties.coordinateEvidence: Reference point inside the reviewed Fort Belle Fontaine Park boundary in quieter-parks.json; original riverside fort site is lost.

properties.title: Missouri legislature meets in St. Charles
properties.description: Missouri legislators first met here on June 4, 1821. St. Charles served as the temporary seat of state government until the move to Jefferson City in 1826.
properties.locationAccuracy: Historic capitol buildings / on-site marker; not the whole former government district.
properties.locationBasis: Historic capitol buildings / on-site marker; not the whole former government district.

properties.title: Jefferson Barracks established
properties.description: Established as an infantry training post in 1826, Jefferson Barracks later served military, hospital and cemetery functions. The historic complex extends well beyond this park reference point.
properties.locationAccuracy: Present-day Jefferson Barracks County Park reference point; the historic military reservation was much larger.
properties.locationBasis: Present-day Jefferson Barracks County Park reference point; the historic military reservation was much larger.

properties.title: Dred and Harriet Scott file freedom suits
properties.description: Dred and Harriet Scott filed separate petitions seeking freedom from slavery in St. Louis. Their local trials took place at the Old Courthouse; the later U.S. Supreme Court decision was made in Washington, D.C.
properties.locationAccuracy: Old Courthouse building location. The pin represents the St. Louis proceedings, not the U.S. Supreme Court decision.
properties.locationBasis: Old Courthouse building location. The pin represents the St. Louis proceedings, not the U.S. Supreme Court decision.

properties.title: Grant family lives and farms at White Haven
properties.description: Ulysses and Julia Grant lived with their family at White Haven during these years. The estate also depended on enslaved African American labor; the National Park Service interprets the lives of both free and enslaved residents.
properties.locationAccuracy: White Haven historic house / interpretive marker; the former farm covered a much larger area.
properties.locationBasis: White Haven historic house / interpretive marker; the former farm covered a much larger area.

properties.title: Camp Jackson Affair
properties.description: Union forces captured the pro-secessionist militia at Camp Jackson. Violence followed as prisoners were marched through St. Louis, and soldiers fired into a civilian crowd.
properties.locationAccuracy: Commemorative marker near Compton and Laclede; not an exact shooting location or the full encampment. Events extended into surrounding streets.
properties.locationBasis: Commemorative marker near Compton and Laclede; not an exact shooting location or the full encampment. Events extended into surrounding streets.

properties.title: Eads Bridge dedicated
properties.description: The road-and-rail bridge across the Mississippi was dedicated on July 4, 1874. Its construction used deep pneumatic caissons and cantilever erection methods.
properties.locationAccuracy: Bridge reference point; not the exact position of the dedication ceremony.
properties.locationBasis: Bridge reference point; not the exact position of the dedication ceremony.
properties.source: City of St. Louis Cultural Resources Office

properties.title: 1896 tornado devastates Lafayette Park
properties.description: The tornado damaged Lafayette Park, toppling trees and wrecking structures including the music pavilion. Destruction extended across other parts of St. Louis and East St. Louis.
properties.locationAccuracy: Documented damaged park / music-pavilion marker. This is one affected location, not the tornado origin or complete track.
properties.locationBasis: Documented damaged park / music-pavilion marker. This is one affected location, not the tornado origin or complete track.

properties.title: 1904 World’s Fair opens
properties.description: The Louisiana Purchase Exposition opened on April 30, 1904. Its extensive grounds occupied western Forest Park and adjacent land; the surviving Palace of Fine Arts is now the Saint Louis Art Museum.
properties.locationAccuracy: Art Museum commemorative marker within the former fair grounds; not an exact opening-ceremony location or the fair boundary.
properties.locationBasis: Art Museum commemorative marker within the former fair grounds; not an exact opening-ceremony location or the fair boundary.

properties.title: 1904 Olympics at Francis Field
properties.description: Francis Field and the adjacent gymnasium hosted a major concentration of the 1904 Olympic competitions. Other Olympic events were held at additional venues and on other dates.
properties.locationAccuracy: Francis Field and Gymnasium commemorative marker; not every 1904 Olympic venue.
properties.locationBasis: Francis Field and Gymnasium commemorative marker; not every 1904 Olympic venue.

properties.title: Gateway Arch construction completed
properties.description: Construction of Eero Saarinen’s Gateway Arch began in 1963 and was completed on October 28, 1965.
properties.locationAccuracy: Gateway Arch grounds reference point; not the elevated final-piece installation position.
properties.locationBasis: Gateway Arch grounds reference point; not the elevated final-piece installation position.
